chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Safwan from Hisham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a free woman whom her slave husband accuses (of adultery), and a free man for whom there is a slave woman under his authority who accuses him. He said: They perform al-li'an (mutual imprecation).
ai.seo_question: Does the ritual of mutual imprecation (li'an) apply when a free woman is married to a slave man?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies that the procedure of al-li'an (mutual imprecation) is universally applicable regardless of the social status disparity between spouses, specifically addressing the unique legal dynamics of a free woman married to a slave or a free man with a slave woman. It underscores the consistency of prophetic jurisprudence in resolving accusations of adultery (zina) within mixed-status unions, ensuring that the evidentiary requirements for divorce and lineage clarification remain uniform. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh for establishing that the master-slave marital bond does not exempt parties from the rigorous four-oath and five-curse protocol outlined in the Quran.
